title: Aligning Large Language Models for Safety in African Languages: A Case Study of Hausa
abstract: arXiv:2610.37245v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Safety alignment research for large language models (LLMs) remains concentrated on high-resource languages, leaving open how existing alignment methods perform in low-resource, culturally distinct settings. We study this question for Hausa, a language spoken by more than 200 million people across West Africa. We introduce HausaSafeLM, one of the first Hausa safety preference dataset, built from 10,000 prompts derived from PKU-SafeRLHF: 3,000 human-corrected (gold) and 7,000 machine-translated (silver) examples spanning six harm macro-categories. translated_title: 面向非洲语言安全的大语言模型对齐：以豪萨语为例的案例研究
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）的安全对齐研究仍然集中于高资源语言，而现有对齐方法在低资源、文化背景迥异的环境中的表现仍是悬而未决的问题。我们针对豪萨语（Hausa）研究这一问题，豪萨语是西非超过两亿人使用的语言。我们提出了HausaSafeLM，这是首批豪萨语安全偏好数据集之一，基于源自PKU-SafeRLHF的10,000条提示构建而成：其中3,000条为人工校正（金标）样本，7,000条为机器翻译（银标）样本，涵盖六大类有害内容宏观类别。我们使用Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct模型，在两种数据条件下比较监督微调（SFT）与SFT后接直接偏好优化（DPO）的效果，并在500条有害和200条良性豪萨语提示上进行评估。我们发现，仅凭拒绝率指标来看，未经调优的基座模型似乎非常安全，但这反映的是其豪萨语生成能力的局限，而非真正的安全对齐：其拒绝行为几乎……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文构建了首批豪萨语安全偏好数据集HausaSafeLM（含3,000条金标和7,000条银标样本），并通过SFT与DPO对比实验揭示：仅凭拒绝率评估低资源语言模型的安全性会产生误导，基座模型的高拒绝率实为豪萨语生成能力不足而非真正的安全对齐。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces HausaSafeLM, one of the first Hausa safety preference datasets (3,000 gold and 7,000 silver examples), and shows through SFT and DPO experiments that refusal-rate metrics alone are misleading, as the untuned base model's high refusal rate reflects limited Hausa generation ability rather than genuine safety alignment.
